problem_statement: netlify-templates auto-annotated-portfolio is a runnable Next.js 15 (pages-router) Stackbit content template rebranded as the portfolio of Ivy Sørensen, a botanical illustrator and herbarium cartographer. The site is composed at build time from Markdown/JSON content under content/ through a shared component design system (HeroSection, FeaturedProjectsSection, ProjectFeedSection/ProjectFeedLayout, ProjectLayout, shared Header/Footer). Its central surface is the plate portfolio: a Home 'Selected plates' teaser and the Plates index at /projects/ that list six commissioned plates (Snow gentian range plate, Coastal saltmarsh field-guide, Herbarium digitisation plates, Arctic saxifrage life-plate, Machair wildflower range map, Fen orchid digitisation set), each with its own detail page. Add and wire a native 'Filter plates by kind' control to the project grid (rendered by ProjectFeedSection): a category tab row [All · Watercolour plates · Range maps · Field guides · Digitisation] and a live readout 'Showing N of M · <Kind>' that sit above the grid. Clicking a category tab must re-render the grid to only the plates of that kind and update the readout count; the control must be present wherever the plate grid appears (the Home teaser, the About page's plate section, and the Plates index) so the filter reads as one continuous feature across the site. The tab row must wrap and the grid must reflow so every page is free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile, and the active tab must stay legible. Keep the shared chrome, layouts and the grounded Ivy Sørensen botanical copy intact — this is an interactive-feature + continuity task, not a content rewrite.
required_content: Add a 'Filter plates by kind' control to the project grid rendered by ProjectFeedSection: a category tab row (All, Watercolour plates, Range maps, Field guides, Digitisation) and a live 'Showing N of M · <Kind>' readout above the grid, using stable classes plate-filter__title / plate-filter__tabs / plate-filter__tab / plate-filter__readout / plate-filter__grid / plate-filter__card-name.

Wire the filter so clicking a category tab re-derives the visible plates from the active tab and rewrites the readout (e.g. clicking 'Range maps' shows 'Showing 2 of 6 · Range maps' and renders only the two range-map plates); the count must never be a snapshot frozen at mount.

Mount the filter wherever the plate grid appears — the Home 'Selected plates' teaser, the About page's 'Selected plates from the herbarium' section, and the Plates index at /projects/ — so the control is continuous across the site rather than appearing on only one route.

Make the tab row wrap and the grid reflow so the Plates index (and every page) is free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile, and keep the active tab legible (no dark-on-dark or clipped/overlapping cards).

Keep the shared component design system, page layouts, header/footer chrome and the grounded Ivy Sørensen botanical plate copy intact across the Home hero, Plates index, project-detail pages and About page.
design_constraints: The plate filter is a native feature of the project grid (ProjectFeedSection): tabs + count sit above the existing grid; do not bolt on an unrelated metric strip.
The filter's visible set and readout must be derived live from the active tab on every render, so clicking a category filters the grid and updates 'Showing N of M · <Kind>'.
The filter must be present on every route that shows the plate grid (Home teaser, About plate section, Plates index) so it reads as one continuous control.
The tab row must wrap and the grid must reflow so no page overflows horizontally on desktop or at 390px mobile, and the active tab must remain legible.
Preserve the shared design system, layouts, chrome and the grounded botanical plate copy; this is an interactive-feature + continuity task, not a demo-content rewrite.

desktop_plates_filter_rangemaps verifies that clicking the 'Range maps' tab re-renders the grid to the two range-map plates and updates the readout to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Range maps'.
desktop_home_filter and desktop_info_filter verify the filter control is also mounted on the Home teaser and the About page's plate section, so it is continuous across the site.
mobile_projects_index and mobile_plates_filter verify the tab row wraps and the grid reflows with no horizontal overflow at 390px.
desktop_project_one/two/three verify each plate detail page keeps its grounded botanical title and body and the shared chrome.

Clicking a category tab re-renders the grid to that kind and updates the count (Range maps -> 'Showing 2 of 6 · Range maps', two cards).

The active tab stays legible and the six grounded plate commissions read as one coherent Ivy Sørensen body of work across the grid and the detail pages.

The grounded botanical plate copy on the detail pages and About page is preserved.

The active tab and readout remain readable on mobile and tablet.

author_notes: L4 harden of the Ivy Sørensen botanical-illustration portfolio. The native lever is a plate category filter built into the project grid (ProjectFeedSection renders a new PlateFilter client component): a 'Filter plates by kind' tab row and a live 'Showing N of M · <Kind>' readout above the six-plate grid. The reference derives the visible set and readout from the live active tab on every render, and mounts the filter on the Home 'Selected plates' teaser, the About page's plate section and the Plates index (/projects/). INFRA (identical all three legs): the build fix pinning glob@8.1.0 (the template's default-import glob.sync breaks under glob@11 on Node 22), the three added plate detail pages (Arctic saxifrage, Machair range map, Fen orchid), the plate category assignments, and the plateFilter content flags. The BASELINE keeps the correct filter WIRING (its click filters the grid and updates the count, so it PASSES the interaction check) but ships the original broken responsive CSS — a fixed-width nowrap tab row and fixed-width nowrap cards that overflow the mobile viewport — and mounts the filter only on the Plates index, so it is missing from the Home teaser and the About page. The BAD solution mounts the filter only on the Plates index AND breaks it two ways: the visible set and readout are snapshotted once at mount (useState initializers) so clicking a tab flips the active-tab class but the grid and count never update (the readout stays frozen at 'Showing all 6 plates' with all six cards shown), and the grid CSS uses a nowrap fixed-width row with negative margins so the cards shingle, overlap and clip off the right edge while the active tab is rendered dark-on-dark and illegible. So the bad solution fails horizontal-overflow (mobile), visual-regression (broken grid), dom-assertions (filter absent on Home and About) and interaction-assertions (frozen count), while the baseline fails the first three but passes the interaction check.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable Next.js 15 pages-router Stackbit portfolio whose central surface is a project grid (ProjectFeedSection on the Home teaser, the About plate section and the Plates index). That grid is the natural, native home for a category filter + result count — the real feature a plate portfolio hosts — making it a clean base for a cross-page design-continuity task where the same interactive filter must be continuous across routes, re-render the grid on click, and stay overflow-free and legible on mobile.
